title: Raw materials
summary: Quartz, silver, copper, aluminum, steel, glass inputs, and specialty minerals enter the chain.

title: Silicon metal and polysilicon
summary: Quartz is reduced to silicon metal, then purified into solar-grade polysilicon.

title: Ingots and wafers
summary: Polysilicon is melted into crystal ingots and sliced into thin wafers.

title: Solar cells
summary: Wafers are textured, doped, coated, and metallized into electricity-producing cells.

title: Module materials and assembly
summary: Cells are wired, sealed between protective layers, framed, tested, and shipped as modules.

title: Trackers and racking
summary: Steel foundations and moving structures hold modules and follow the sun.

title: Inverters and controls
summary: Power electronics convert module output from direct current into grid-ready alternating current.

title: Electrical balance of system
summary: Cable, combiner boxes, switchgear, and transformers collect power and connect the plant to the grid.

title: Installed U.S. project
summary: Manufactured equipment becomes an operating U.S. solar plant and sets the annual demand for the chain.

title: CdTe comparison
summary: Thin semiconductor layers deposited on glass replace the polysilicon, wafer, and separate cell stages.
